disclosure: Recorded before viewing generator_calibration_v1 beyond cluster_bridge n <= 2000 and before any calibration of candidate redesigns. Already seen and stated when proposing these rules: v1 cluster_bridge fails R1 and R2 on n <= 2000; v1 D3 is expected to fail R2 for a stated mathematical reason (fixed sigma, n/8 points per hotspot).
principle: A geometry in the balanced primary factorial must respond meaningfully to the declared density parameter and must preserve a broadly comparable local-degree regime as n changes (owner's statement). Literature direction (to verify against full text): keep the thermodynamic regime (finite mean degree) by growing the spatial domain with n rather than crowding fixed regions.
applies_to: every geometry proposed for the primary factorial (sizes 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000; densities 8, 12), in addition to gates_v1 G1 (and G2/G3 for the clustered geometry)

R1_density_response.rule: at every n: median mean degree at density 12 / at density 8 >= 1.25

R2_scale_stability.rule: within each density: max_n / min_n of the median mean degree <= 2 over all tested n

R3_bottleneck_character.applies_to: the bottleneck geometry (dumbbell / cluster_bridge successor) only
R3_bottleneck_character.rule: corridor width <= r (=1) and the corridor holds < 10% of the points at every n
R3_bottleneck_character.wording_provenance: The locked rule is 'corridor width <= r' (max_corridor_width 1.0, inclusive), as written in this file at ~12:09:00Z. Three minutes earlier (12:05:45Z) the assistant had proposed 'bridge strip width < r' (strict) in discussion; the change to <= was made by the assistant when recording the requirements and was not flagged as a change. The single dumbbell candidate (w = 1.0, l = 3.0) was chosen afterwards by the assistant from two proposed candidates. w = 1.0 lies exactly on the bound: under the strict wording the dumbbell would have failed R3. The project owner directed that the rule as locked before calibration governs; it is applied unchanged.

decision_rule: A candidate that meets G1 and R1-R3 (and, for clustered, G2/G3) may replace the v1 generator; among passing candidates, prefer the one closest to the owner's stated design intent, decided before final data. If no bottleneck candidate passes, cluster_bridge leaves the primary factorial and becomes a separate bottleneck stress-test study. Requirements are never loosened after viewing results; candidates are calibrated on new independent validation seeds.
